title: Crossing
description: A summer photograph of a Japanese level crossing that turns out to be built like a paper diorama. Drag, or tilt your phone, and it comes apart into its real depth planes: the sky card stands back, the poles and wires hang in the middle, the near signal floats forward, each a cut-out with the street continued behind it, throwing soft skylight shadows on the cards behind. The lens focuses on whichever plane is under your finger. Let go and it closes back into one flat photograph.
intent: Multiple layers of an image, the physical world inside the computer. After Disney's multiplane camera (1937, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplane_camera) and paper tunnel books (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_book): one photo cut offline into seven matted, inpainted planes that separate in z with true perspective, each scaled so that from the lens axis the stack is still exactly the photograph.

sources.author: XS Xue (@xxs11)
